production.note: US model years 2019-2020. Start: Autoblog (Sven Gustafson, 29 March 2018), "Ford has opened order books for the 2019 Mustang Bullitt." End: Autoblog (Ben Hsu, 1 February 2021), "so the final car is a 2020 model, coming off the heels of a two-year production run." (source autoblog-bullitt-ends-2021).

body.note: Panel: "VEHICLE TYPE: front-engine, rear-wheel-drive, 4-passenger, 2-door coupe". Fastback only: Autoblog calls it a "commemorative-edition GT fastback" (source autoblog-bullitt-2019).

configuration.note: Coyote. Panel: "ENGINE TYPE: DOHC 32-valve V-8, aluminum block and heads, port and direct fuel injection".

aspiration.note: Inferred: the panel's engine line names no supercharger or turbocharger (C&D prints "supercharged and intercooled" or "turbocharged" where they exist).

fuel.note: Inferred from the panel's engine line.

transmission.note: Panel: "TRANSMISSION: 6-speed manual". Manual only: Autoblog, "there's no automatic option" (source autoblog-bullitt-2019); The Drive (Chris Tsui, 2 February 2021), "was hooked up exclusively to a six-speed manual transmission" (source thedrive-final-bullitt-2021).

powerHp.note: Car and Driver road-test panel, 2019 Bullitt. Quote: "POWER: 480 hp @ 7000 rpm". Autoblog: Ford "confirmed final output for the commemorative-edition GT fastback at 480 horsepower and 420 pound-feet of torque." (source autoblog-bullitt-2019); The Drive: "the Bullitt's 5.0-liter Coyote V8 made 480 horsepower" (source thedrive-final-bullitt-2021), so the rating held for 2020.

weightLb.note: Car and Driver road-test curb weight, 2019 Bullitt fastback with the 6-speed manual (the only transmission; base $47,590, as tested $52,980). Quote: "Curb weight: 3850 lb".
